2Easy

Starting from the budget line with p1=1p_1 = 1p1​=1, p2=2p_2 = 2p2​=2, w=100w = 100w=100, how does the budget line move when www rises to 150150150? Find the new optimum of a Cobb-Douglas consumer with a=1/2a = 1/2a=1/2.

  • Utility Maximization
Show solution
  1. A pure income rise shifts the budget line outward in parallel: intercepts move from (100,50)(100, 50)(100,50) to (150,75)(150, 75)(150,75).
  2. Demand is proportional to wealth, so x1=0.5⋅150/1=75x_1 = 0.5 \cdot 150/1 = 75x1​=0.5⋅150/1=75, x2=0.5⋅150/2=37.5x_2 = 0.5 \cdot 150/2 = 37.5x2​=0.5⋅150/2=37.5 — exactly 1.51.51.5 times the original (50,25)(50, 25)(50,25).

Hard

5Hard

Prove with the Slutsky equation that a Giffen good cannot arise under Cobb-Douglas utility.

∂x1∂p1=∂h1∂p1−∂x1∂wx1\frac{\partial x_1}{\partial p_1} = \frac{\partial h_1}{\partial p_1} - \frac{\partial x_1}{\partial w} x_1∂p1​∂x1​​=∂p1​∂h1​​−∂w∂x1​​x1​
  • The Slutsky Decomposition
Show solution
  1. In Cobb-Douglas, ∂x1/∂w=a/p1>0\partial x_1/\partial w = a/p_1 > 0∂x1​/∂w=a/p1​>0 — good 1 is always normal. So the income effect −(∂x1/∂w)x1-(\partial x_1/\partial w) x_1−(∂x1​/∂w)x1​ is always negative.
  2. The substitution effect ∂h1/∂p1≤0\partial h_1/\partial p_1 \le 0∂h1​/∂p1​≤0 is also never positive (compensated law of demand), so the total effect is a sum of two negatives — always negative. A Giffen good (∂x1/∂p1>0\partial x_1/\partial p_1 > 0∂x1​/∂p1​>0) is impossible.
6Hard

Prove the duality identity e(p,v(p,w))=we(p, v(p, w)) = we(p,v(p,w))=w from the definitions of the UMP and EMP (assume interior solutions and local nonsatiation).

v(p,w)=max⁡p⋅x≤wu(x),e(p,u)=min⁡u(x)≥up⋅xv(p, w) = \max_{p \cdot x \le w} u(x), \qquad e(p, u) = \min_{u(x) \ge u} p \cdot xv(p,w)=p⋅x≤wmax​u(x),e(p,u)=u(x)≥umin​p⋅x
  • Expenditure Minimization and Duality
  • Utility Maximization
Show solution
  1. Let x∗=x(p,w)x^* = x(p, w)x∗=x(p,w) solve the UMP. By local nonsatiation p⋅x∗=wp \cdot x^* = wp⋅x∗=w and u(x∗)=v(p,w)u(x^*) = v(p, w)u(x∗)=v(p,w). Since x∗x^*x∗ is feasible for the EMP at target utility v(p,w)v(p,w)v(p,w), e(p,v(p,w))≤p⋅x∗=we(p, v(p, w)) \le p \cdot x^* = we(p,v(p,w))≤p⋅x∗=w.
  2. Conversely, if e(p,v(p,w))<we(p, v(p,w)) < we(p,v(p,w))<w, the EMP solution yyy satisfies p⋅y<wp \cdot y < wp⋅y<w and u(y)≥v(p,w)u(y) \ge v(p, w)u(y)≥v(p,w). Local nonsatiation gives a nearby feasible bundle with even higher uuu, contradicting the maximality of v(p,w)v(p, w)v(p,w). Hence equality holds.
